web-guide-idea-3.audience: Travellers, former residents and Indians abroad who miss the riverfront.
web-guide-idea-3.offer: Host an evening at one specific ghat, combining changing light with local stories. Your familiarity helps viewers understand what they are seeing.
web-guide-idea-3.steps.0: Scout a permitted spot with usable signal.
web-guide-idea-3.steps.1: Introduce the ghat before sunset and explain the evening’s activity.
web-guide-idea-3.steps.2: Hold a steady view as lamps appear, then answer questions from a quiet spot.
web-guide-idea-3.equipment: A phone, power bank and small grip or tripod where allowed. Clear sound matters more than cinematic equipment.
web-guide-idea-3.returnReason: Return at different seasons and introduce another ghat’s history. A recognisable host makes the place feel familiar across visits.
web-guide-idea-3.promotion: Use a sunset still with the ghat’s name and a specific story you will tell. State that weather and permitted viewpoints can affect coverage.

web-guide-idea-3.metadataDescription: Share an evening by the ghats, local stories and permitted ceremony coverage with a distant audience. Learn what to offer, how to start and what equipment you need.
